newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian gold jewellery output falls in Q2 1996.
newsitem.headline: Italian gold jewellery output falls in Q2 1996.

text.p: Italian gold jewellery production fell 4.4 percent to 159.3 tonnes in the second quarter of this year against the same 1995 period, Federorafi, the national federation of goldsmiths and jewellery makers, said.
Italy is the world's leader in gold jewellery making.
Federorafi said in a statement that based on World Gold Council data, production in the first half of this year declined by 3.0 percent while domestic consumption dropped 10 percent.

But Italy's market share of exports to the U.S., its main overseas market, rose slightly in the first quarter to 41.06 percent from 39.01 percent in the same 1995 period, for a total value of 372 billion lire.
Federorafi chairman Agostino Roverato said the trend in the sector was very negative with businesses reporting disappointing production levels.
"Even more worrying is the trend in the domestic market where demand is reflecting the general climate of uncertainty which is inevitably holding down consumption," he said.

While forecasts for the sector could not be described as optimistic, he said, jewellery makers were looking forward to the autumn period, which traditionally shows an upturn in orders ahead of Christmas.
